reviewer: AI (Claude), independent of the author; not a native-speaker or teacher review

scope.notes: Read all 94 pool items (37 reading, 6 dialogue, 40 standalone connective/coherence items, 11 sentence items) and the expanded dump (253 questions). SYSTEMIC ISSUES (no per-item patch, fix in authoring): (1) every passage is only 55-94 words (most 75-90) while SPEC asks 120-250 for H; (2) in the non-cloze reading questions the correct option is the longest in 120 of 150 (80%) and in 25 of 25 main-idea questions - a strong length giveaway; the pair-cloze questions are balanced, correct positions are evenly spread (0-3); (3) many passages are easy for H1 (grade 2 band 'd' items such as the notice, recipe, restaurant dialogue) and nearly all follow the same frame 'Which pair best fills (A) and (B)? / What is the passage mainly about? / detail / vocabulary'; (4) topic repeats: volunteering x3 (16, 19, 28), notices/emails x6; (5) std 12영Ⅰ-01-04 on grammar-level clause items (Despite/Although/so...that) is generous. Connective-cloze answers were otherwise checked individually; apart from the patched ones, each has one defensible answer among the options offered (the author avoided offering near-synonyms together, e.g. never both However and Nevertheless). Standalone coherence items (60-64) are much easier than suneung irrelevant-sentence/insertion items; insertion items 27, 63, 64 each have one defensible position.

set.text: I started learning the guitar six months ago, and my progress has been slower than I hoped. Although I practice for thirty minutes every day, my fingers still hurt, and some chords sound terrible. My teacher says this is normal and tells me not to feel discouraged. (A) giving up, she suggests that I record myself once a week. When I listen to old recordings, I can hear how much I have improved. That small habit has changed my attitude, and I now look forward to practice rather than dreading it.

patches.why: Q1 is flawed: with the stem '(A) of getting discouraged', 'Because' makes the grammatical, sensible 'Because of getting discouraged, she suggests ...' (teacher reacts to the writer's discouragement), and 'In spite' + of is unnatural but 'Besides' was also not clearly excluded; two readings. Rewritten so only 'Instead of' fits ('giving up'); 'discouraged' kept in an earlier sentence for the vocabulary question. Q3 option 'Recording himself or herself' is awkward/odd English (the teacher suggests the writer record himself/herself, and the teacher is 'she'); replaced with a neutral paraphrase.

set.q:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) The Han River is a popular place for leisure in Seoul. (2) Many families have picnics along its banks. (3) Many cyclists ride along the paths beside the water. (4) Calculators were first sold in the 1960s.

patches.why: 'The river is also known for its fish-shaped boats' is an invented, false-sounding fact about the Han River; sentence (3) should be a plain on-topic sentence. (Item is also very easy: the off-topic sentence is absurd, unlike suneung irrelevant-sentence items.)

o: In contrast, it breaks down within a few weeks.
Otherwise, many countries have banned plastic bags.
Similarly, glass bottles are made from sand.
Therefore, reducing its use helps the environment.

patches.why: Distractors such as 'Meanwhile, I had lunch yesterday' and 'red toys are popular' are absurd, so the item is solved without reading the connective; replaced with on-topic sentences whose connectives are logically wrong.

Duplicate of the sentence item 'Although it rained, we went hiking' (cloze Although/Despite/Because) - same learning point.
Near-duplicate of 'Despite the heavy rain, the game continued' (Despite + noun phrase, rain frame).
Duplicate of the 'Because of the storm, ...' sentence item (because of + noun phrase).
Duplicate of the 'She was so tired that ...' sentence item (so ... that); also middle-school level.
Duplicate of 'He was late because he missed the train.' (because + clause).
Same Unless lesson as 'Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.'
Same whereas lesson as 'Whereas Tom likes tea, Mia prefers coffee.'
Duplicate of the result-connective item with 'Consequently' (cause then result); too easy for H1.
Middle-school level (so/because/but); trivial for H1.
Meta-question whose answer ('For instance' = Example) is given away by the item name and is trivial for H1.

criteria: Passages must meet the SPEC length for the level (H: 120-250 words); a 55-90 word passage is too thin for suneung-style connective/flow items.

For every connective cloze, test each distractor in the blank AND with its sentence neighbours: 'Because/Although', 'although/so', 'In contrast/Therefore' often produce a second sensible reading when the clause is about a purpose or consequence. Never put a concession and a cause conjunction together unless the context excludes one explicitly.
Do not offer a distractor that is merely a different word for the same relation (However/Nevertheless/Still, For example/For instance, Moreover/In addition/Also, Therefore/As a result/Thus).
Make correct answers shorter or equal in length to distractors in main-idea and detail questions; in this packet the key was the longest option in 80% of such questions.
Vary question frames: do not ask 'Which pair best fills (A) and (B)?' + 'What is the passage mainly about?' for 30 passages; add true/false, reference, inference, order and insertion questions.
Irrelevant-sentence / insertion distractors must be on-topic and subtle, never absurd ('I had lunch yesterday'); do not invent facts (fish-shaped boats) for filler sentences.
Do not write several standalone items with the same frame and answer (Although/Despite + rain, because/because of + noun, so...that, Unless, whereas); one per grammar point per packet.
std tags must describe what the student actually does (reading a letter is not 'writing a letter'); keep cultural-attitude tags for items that really discuss culture.
Ordinary ad-hoc phrases like 'Recording himself or herself' or a dialogue answer with 'too' that has no antecedent are wording defects: read each option aloud against the text.
